text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and have you noticed any pain or swelling in your legs? I need to rule out endometritis and deep vein thrombosis.

text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that the WBC results are pending, but the clinical picture of fever, uterine tenderness, and prolonged labor strongly suggests postpartum endometritis. I will request a blood culture and start empiric antibiotics while we wait for the lab results. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative workup for sepsis, urinary tract infection, and pulmonary embolism, combined with your fever, uterine tenderness, and history of prolonged labor, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis
